The Serra Residences sells 18.8% at launch, with average price of $3,460 psf
article:
Far East Organization has sold 25 of the 133 units at The Serra Residences , or 18.8%, since bookings opened on Oct 16. Transacted prices ranged from $3,123 to $4,200 psf, with an average of $3,460 psf, according to the developer.

The freehold condo on Bassein Road in District 11 is a redevelopment of the former Pastoral View and an adjacent vacant plot. It is a short walk from Novena MRT Station.

The top price was set by the larger of two penthouses, a 2,669 sq ft unit that sold for $11.21 million, or $4,200 psf.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The other units sold comprised nine two-bedroom plus study units, two three-bedroom units, seven four-bedroom units and six four- and five-bedroom premium units.

About 80% of buyers are purchasing for their own use, says Far East Organization in a statement. Singaporeans account for 75% of buyers, and the rest are Singapore permanent residents (PRs) originally from Australia, Britain, China, the Philippines and Taiwan. Buyers include business owners and professionals in the medical, banking and finance, and legal sectors.

“Investors also recognise the long-term rental potential anchored by the expanding HealthCity Novena precinct and the upcoming 2 Moulmein Road lifestyle hub,” the developer adds. The Serra Residences’ connectivity to Orchard Road and the CBD also gives it a broad pool of potential tenants.

The Serra is a single 28-storey tower. Levels four to 16 hold two-bedroom plus study units of 710 to 721 sq ft, three-bedroom units of 764 to 904 sq ft, and four-bedroom units of 958 sq ft.

The Summit , on levels 18 to 28, holds larger four-bedroom units of 1,216 to 1,528 sq ft, five-bedroom premium units of 1,755 sq ft, and the two penthouses of 2,648 and 2,669 sq ft.

title: Thomson Reserve draws 11,800 visitors at preview, highest turnout this year
article:
Thomson Reserve drew 11,800 visitors over its preview weekend of Oct 17–18, the highest turnout this year, ahead of bookings opening on Oct 31.

This surpasses the 10,000 visitors recorded at ParkTown Residence ’s preview last year, said a spokesperson for joint developers UOL Group and CapitaLand Development (CLD).

“It underscores the appeal of a rare five-hectare private residential development offering excellent connectivity, extensive greenery and spacious, upscale homes in the established Upper Thomson neighbourhood,” the spokesperson added.

At 1,268 units, Thomson Reserve is the first project with more than 1,000 units to launch this year.

The spokesperson added that the project’s location, product offering and limited supply nearby have drawn strong interest across unit types from an islandwide pool of buyers. These include first-time homeowners and young families with school-going children, as well as multi-generational families and right-sizers. Younger buyers looking to live near their parents have also shown interest. Ai Tong School is within 1km of the development.

The project is developed by a consortium of CLD, which holds a 50% stake, UOL Group (40%) and UOL’s subsidiary Singapore Land Group (10%). It is a redevelopment of the former Thomson View, which the consortium acquired en bloc in November 2024 for $810 million. The purchase price translated to $1,178 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr), after factoring in land betterment charges and the premium to top up the lease to a fresh 99 years.

The 5ha site, about the size of seven football fields, has a 500m frontage along Upper Thomson Road and is a two-minute walk from Upper Thomson MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

Designed by P&T Consultants, the six residential towers occupy just 12% of the site. The remaining 88% is dedicated to landscaping, water features, and recreational facilities designed by Ecoplan Asia.

More than 45% of residential stacks face the Central Catchment Nature Reserve, and over 80% overlook either greenery or the development’s internal landscaping.

Thomson Reserve has two residential collections. The Classic Collection has 740 units across four 21-storey towers, offering two- to four-bedroom layouts. The Luxury Collection has 528 units in two 30-storey towers, ranging from two-bedroom premium units to five-bedroom suites. Of these, 112 larger four-bedroom premium units and five-bedroom suites have private lift access.

Two-bedroom units make up the bulk of the project, at 716 units or 56.5%. They range from 592 to 775 sq ft, with prices from $1.544 million ($2,608 psf).

There are 350 three-bedroom units (27.6%) of 947 to 1,152 sq ft, priced from $2.503 million ($2,643 psf).

The 174 four-bedroom units (13.7%) range from 1,238 to 1,485 sq ft, with prices from $3.388 million ($2,737 psf).

At the top end are 28 five-bedroom suites of 1,808 sq ft each, making up 2.2% of the development. They occupy a single stack with unblocked views towards MacRitchie Reservoir and the Orchard Road skyline.

ParkTown Residence, the same consortium's 1,193-unit integrated development in Tampines North, sold 1,041 units, or 87%, over its launch weekend in February 2025, at an average of $2,360 psf. It is now 98% sold.
